source.title: Subthalamic nucleus stimulation reverses mediofrontal influence over decision threshold

confidence_rationale: Causal human intervention (STN-DBS ON/OFF within-subject) plus EEG + drift-diffusion modeling showing the STN dynamically modulates the decision/commitment threshold in real time and that disrupting the STN removes the brake (impulsive responding). Directly evidences that the STN/beta substrate -- the SAME circuit as the MECH-090 beta gate -- is a continuously-modulated bidirectional commitment regulator, not a one-shot admission latch. Mapping fidelity high for the 'beta gate is dynamic, not latch-only' claim; the DBS perturbation is a strong causal handle.
failure_signatures: STN-DBS removing the conflict-adaptive threshold elevation produces IMPULSIVE premature responding -- the clinical signature of a missing/disabled maintenance brake. The mirror failure (a too-aggressive maintenance brake) is perseverative over-holding.

The STN threshold modulation is conflict/evidence-graded and operates over the deliberation window, not a categorical post-hoc release -- another data point against a one-shot Schmitt-flag implementation at the latch.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Medial prefrontal theta (4-8 Hz) scales the decision threshold up in proportion to decision conflict on high-conflict trials (P=0.01); STN deep-brain stimulation reverses this mPFC-theta-to-threshold relationship (P=0.045), speeding responses and producing impulsive choice. The STN buys time for cortico-striatal systems to settle on the best choice under conflict ('hold your horses').
mapping.ree_translation: The STN, which IS the basal-ganglia substrate of the MECH-090 beta gate, dynamically and bidirectionally modulates the commitment threshold in real time as a function of ongoing conflict/decisiveness -- and removing it causes premature, impulsive commitment. This refutes the reading that admission-only is the biologically correct architecture for the beta-gate latch (option iii / B3c): the same circuit that admits a commitment continuously regulates whether it should be held or released. It supports siting a maintenance-time, decisiveness-driven release coupling AT the R-c / beta-gate level (autopsy option (a), resurfacing under B3b).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Cavanagh's threshold modulation is measured during pre-response deliberation (gating commitment ENTRY timing), not explicitly during an already-elevated committed motor program. It establishes the STN/beta gate is a continuously-modulated bidirectional regulator (against admission-only) and is the same circuit as REE's gate, but it does not by itself demonstrate release of an already-initiated program -- that is the Resulaj entry's contribution. The two compose.
mapping.source_context: Human Parkinson's-disease patients with STN-DBS, within-subject ON/OFF; scalp EEG theta + Hierarchical Drift Diffusion Model; high- vs low-conflict reinforcement-learning choices.

confidence_components.notes: Strong causal design (within-subject DBS ON/OFF) in humans, Nature Neuroscience. Mapping_fidelity 0.72: directly supports 'STN/beta gate is dynamic+bidirectional, not admission-only' but the threshold is studied at entry-timing, not mid-program maintenance. Transfer_risk 0.38: PD-DBS cohort + conflict-RL task to REE latch.
